title: Efficient Training of Boltzmann Generators Using Off-Policy Log-Dispersion Regularization
claim: A dispersion-based shape regularizer on the log-density gap, added to data-based training losses, aligns the model with the target landscape.
layout: 2 panels; (a) stacked plots with equations, (b) left-to-right training arrow with shaded optional inset
description: Panel (a), on the left, introduces the log-dispersion objective. A top 1-D plot shows a blue double-well target curve, -log p̃_X, above a red proposal curve, -log q_X^θ, with a vertical bar marking their gap. An arrow leads from the bar to the definition f^θ(x) = -log q - (-log p̃) and the loss L_LD^θ(p) = E_{x~r_X}[|f^θ(x) - E_r[f^θ(x)]|^p]. A lower orange plot of f^θ(x) shows a dashed mean line with shaded deviations. Panel (b), on the right, shows training. A target-sample plot with blue dots on the double-well sits at upper left. A thick 'Training' arrow, labeled with L_data and the L_LD term, leads to a red 'Trained model' curve. A grey rounded box holds an optional biased-sample plot with green dots. Color coding ties the notation to the plots: blue is target, red is proposal, orange is f, green is biased samples.
caption: (a) The log-dispersion objective minimizes the dispersion of $f^\theta(x)=-\log q_X^\theta(x) -(-\log \tilde{p}_X(x))$ around its mean, regularizing the shape of the proposal $q_X^\theta$ over the support of a reference distribution $r_X$. (b) When training off-policy, e.g., with a fixed dataset, log-dispersion alone is not a divergence because it does not constrain the proposal outside the support of $r_X$. We therefore use log-dispersion as a shape regularizer on top of data-based divergences to ensure global normalization. Since the reference distribution $r_X$ is flexible, LDR can be applied to target samples $x_i\sim p_X$ as well as biased samples $x_i^{biased}\sim p_X^{biased}$.
abstract: Sampling from unnormalized probability densities is a central challenge in computational science. Boltzmann generators are generative models that enable independent sampling from the Boltzmann distribution of physical systems at a given temperature. However, their practical success depends on data-efficient training, as both simulation data and target energy evaluations are costly. To this end, we propose off-policy log-dispersion regularization (LDR), a novel regularization framework that builds on a generalization of the log-variance objective. We apply LDR in the off-policy setting in combination with standard data-based training objectives, without requiring additional on-policy samples. LDR acts as a shape regularizer of the energy landscape by leveraging additional information in the form of target energy labels. The proposed regularization framework is broadly applicable, supporting unbiased or biased simulation datasets as well as purely variational training without access to target samples. Across all benchmarks, LDR improves both final performance and data efficiency, with sample efficiency gains of up to one order of magnitude.
